inscription: RAF badge: PER ARDUA AD ASTRA. THIS MEMORIAL IS DEDICATED TO THE AIRMEN WHO TRAGICALLY LOST THEIR LIVES ON 28th DECEMBER 1942 WHILST FLYING THEIR WELLINGTON BOMBER BK517 WHICH CAME DOWN NEAR THIS SITE. Fg Off John G Byrne RAFVR; FS Jack T McDonald RCAF; FS William McMillan RAFVR; LAC Leslie H Nicholson RAFVR; AC2 John G Beaumont RAFVR; AC2 Granville Broadhurst RAFVR
cause_of_loss: Hit an elm tree while flying low in bad weather; the cause was not established
erected_by: Bodicote Parish Council, the village of Bodicote and other local people
narrative:
On 28 December 1942 Vickers Wellington III BK517 of 23 Operational Training Unit crashed in fields near Bodicote, Oxfordshire. All six men on board died. The flight was an air test described on the accident card as an Air Test (Medical), planned to last about 25 minutes, and is believed to have begun at RAF Atherstone-on-Stour. Sources give different take-off times: Aircrew Remembered says 11:20, the Fulwood History Group about 11:30.

There was no wireless operator on board. The accident card says the aircraft flew into cloud and crashed while trying to make landfall in bad weather. A schoolboy and his mother saw it pass very low from the south-east with one engine apparently smoking, and he saw it hit an elm tree, lose a wing and crash into the valley beyond.

Investigators from the Midland Aircraft Recovery Group later examined the site and spoke to the eyewitness. They concluded the aircraft was flying level and fast, and that the smoke could have been an exhaust trail at full throttle. No investigation established a cause. The Fulwood History Group describes the card as saying the aircraft was attempting to land.

The six men were Flying Officer John Gordon Byrne (22), Flight Sergeant Jack Thompson McDonald (26, Royal Canadian Air Force), Flight Sergeant William McMillan (26), Leading Aircraftman Leslie Hamilton Nicholson (20), and Aircraftmen 2nd Class John Ernest George Beaumont (19) and Granville Broadhurst (19). Byrne was an experienced flying instructor from Fulwood, Sheffield, and had been married about 13 weeks. He is buried at Fulwood, McDonald at Middleton Stoney, McMillan at Greenock, Nicholson at Rotherham, Beaumont at Brompton Cemetery in London and Broadhurst at Erdington, Birmingham.
community_connection: Bodicote Parish Council is responsible for the memorial, and the memorial's administrator manages its administration, history and events. Two ceremonies are held each year at 10:45: an Act of Remembrance on Remembrance Sunday, and a commemoration with an Act of Remembrance on 28 December, the anniversary of the crash. The 2012 unveiling was attended by Byrne's widow, then aged 92, his brother and many other relatives of the crew, including a niece of Beaumont.
memorial_details: The memorial is a block of Hornton stone with an engraved bronze plaque, unveiled and dedicated on 2 June 2012. The plaque carries the RAF badge, a dedication to the airmen who lost their lives on 28 December 1942 flying Wellington BK517, and the names of the six crew. It stands about 400 metres south of Wykham Lane across two fields, with permissive access from the lane, and is enclosed by a circular metal railing fence. IWM records its condition as good. It was erected by Bodicote Parish Council, the village of Bodicote and other local people.
